Circled Dot Operator Symbol

There is no legacy Windows Alt code for Circled Dot Operator because it is not in either the OEM code page 437 or Windows-1252 tables. The Unicode codepoint is U+2299, which you can use as ⊙ in HTML, \2299 in CSS, or type with Alt+8857 on Windows (BMP only). If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, use the Character Viewer, the HTML entity, or copy the character directly. Circled Dot Operator is outside both legacy code pages, which is why U+2299 is the identifier that works across Word, HTML, CSS, Python and JavaScript. Circled Dot Operator has no named HTML entity, so use the numeric escape ⊙ or the hex escape ⊙.

How to type circled dot operator on Windows

  1. Turn Num Lock on so the numeric keypad is active.
  2. Hold the left Alt key.
  3. Type 8 8 5 7 on the numeric keypad for the decimal codepoint 8857.
  4. Release Alt. The Circled Dot Operator character (⊙) appears.

If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, see how to type symbols without a numpad.

How to type circled dot operator on macOS

There is no direct Option shortcut for Circled Dot Operator. Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space, search for "Circled Dot Operator" and click the character to insert it.

How to use circled dot operator in code

  • HTML: or
  • CSS: content:"\2299"; ()
  • Python: \u2299 or chr(0x2299)
  • JavaScript: \u2299 or String.fromCodePoint(0x2299)
  • JSON: "\u2299"

Frequently asked questions

Is there an Alt code for ⊙?

No legacy Alt code exists for Circled Dot Operator because it is not in code page 437 or Windows-1252. Use the Unicode codepoint U+2299 in HTML, CSS or the Character Viewer instead.

How do I type ⊙ without a numpad?

Use the Windows Character Viewer (Win+.), the macOS Character Viewer (⌃⌘Space), an HTML entity such as ⊙, or copy the character directly from this page.

Why does Alt+8857 not work?

Alt+8857 only works on a keyboard with a physical numeric keypad. It also requires the application to accept the numeric-keypad input path. Laptops without a numpad need an alternative method.

What is the Unicode for Circled Dot Operator?

The Unicode codepoint for Circled Dot Operator is U+2299. You can use this value in HTML as ⊙, in CSS as \2299, and in Word with Alt+X.

How do I type ⊙ on a Mac?

Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space and search for the character name or U+2299, then click it.
